'''Jean-Marc Deshouillers''' (born on September 12, 1946<ref>Henryk Iwaniec: ''The sixtieth birthday of Jean-Marc Deshouillers.'' In: ''Functiones et Approximatio Commentarii Mathematici.'' Volume 37, nr. 1, 2007, pp. 7–16 ([http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.facm/1229618737 online] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004230109/http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.facm%2F1229618737 |date=2013-10-04 }})</ref> in [[Paris]]) is a French mathematician, specializing in [[analytic number theory]]. He is a professor at the [[University of Bordeaux]].

==Education and career==
Deshouillers attended the Paris [[École Polytechnique]],<ref name="AX">He belongs to the X1965 promotion, cf. [http://kx.polytechniciens.com/?page=AX_FICHE_ANCIEN&ancc_id=19650087 the website of the ''association des anciens élèves de l'École polytechnique (the AX)''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402155304/http://kx.polytechniciens.com/?page=AX_FICHE_ANCIEN&ancc_id=19650087 |date=2015-04-02 }} (the old fellows association).</ref><ref name="Polytech.Fiche">[http://www.bibliotheque.polytechnique.edu/jsp/accueil.jsp?CODE=64303226&LANGUE=1 Website of the library of the École Polytechnique] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150302142412/http://www.bibliotheque.polytechnique.edu/jsp/accueil.jsp?CODE=64303226&LANGUE=1 |date=2015-03-02 }}, thumb index « ''BCX Catalogs –> Polytechnicien family'' », search for « Jean-Marc Deshouillers », you get : « Deshouillers, Jean-Marc (X 1965) ».</ref> graduating with an engineer diploma in 1968.

He received his PhD in 1972 at the [[Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University|University Paris VI ''Pierre et Marie Curie'']].

In the seventies, he was assistant professor in mathematics at the École Polytechnique, which moved from Paris to [[Palaiseau]].

Deshouillers is a professor at the University of Bordeaux. In 2009 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].

==Contributions==
In 1985 he showed with [[Ramachandran Balasubramanian]] and François Dress that, in the case of the fourth powers of [[Waring's problem]], the least number of fourth powers that is necessary to express any positive integer as a sum of fourth powers is 19.<ref>''Problème de Waring pour les bicarrés.'' In: ''Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des sciences.'' Volume 303, 1986, pp. 85, 161</ref>

With [[Henryk Iwaniec]], he improved the Kuznetsov trace formula.<ref>''Kloosterman sums and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.'' In: ''Inventiones Mathematicae.'' Volume 70, 1982, pp. 219–288</ref> In 1997, with Effinger and Herman te Riele, he proved the [[ternary Goldbach conjecture]] (every odd number greater than 5 is a sum of three [[prime number]]s) under the [[Generalized Riemann Hypothesis]].<ref>''A complete Vinogradov 3-primes theorem under the Riemann hypothesis.'' In: ''Electronic Research Announcements of the AMS.'' Volume 3, 1997, pp. 99–104, 17. September 1997</ref> Together with [[François Dress]] and [[Gérald Tenenbaum]] he discovered the [[DDT theorem]].

Among his students was [[Gérald Tenenbaum]].
